summary: Bun Rany Hun Sen, President of the Cambodian Red Cross, has approved emergency humanitarian aid for 2,880 families currently residing in safety camps in Banteay Meanchey province. These families were displaced due to ongoing border tensions. The aid includes essential food supplies and materials to support those who have not yet been able to return to their homes along the border line.
title: Cambodian Red Cross to Provide Emergency Aid to 2,880 Displaced Families in Banteay Meanchey

summary: The Ministry of Interior reports that nearly 600,000 residents (92%) displaced by recent border tensions have returned home. However, over 49,000 people remain displaced. The ministry noted that while the Dec 27 ceasefire holds, essential services like schools and hospitals in Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Preah Vihear provinces remain closed. Cambodia continues to monitor 'dishonest activities' by Thai forces, including the deployment of containers and barbed wire in disputed zones.
title: 92% of Displaced Border Residents Return Home, 49,352 Still Await Resettlement: Interior Ministry

summary: Phnom Penh has proposed the deployment of joint survey teams to resume installing boundary markers in disputed areas of Battambang and Banteay Meanchey. Government spokesperson Pen Bona rejected Thai allegations that Cambodia used Preah Vihear Temple as a military base, clarifying that barbed wire was installed only to prevent Thai encroachment after the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) saw illegal construction by the Thai side near the temple gate.
title: Cambodia calls for border demarcation talks with Thailand, rejects temple militarisation claims

summary: Acting Head of State Hun Sen has sent a message to international leaders—particularly those from Europe—reassuring them that the border dispute with Thailand will not impact their safety during the 20th Francophonie Summit (OIF) hosted by Cambodia in late 2026. He stated that despite current border issues, the situation will not interfere with the organization of this major historic event.
title: Samdech Techo Tells World Leaders Attending Francophonie Meeting in Cambodia Not to Worry About Safety

summary: Senate President Hun Sen met with the Secretary-General of the International Organization of the Francophonie (OIF) on Monday morning. During the meeting, he assured international leaders that the ongoing border tensions and territorial disputes with Thailand would not affect the security or success of the upcoming Francophonie Summit, which Cambodia will host in late November 2026. He emphasized that Cambodia is experienced in maintaining peace and stability despite external regional challenges.
title: Samdech Techo Hun Sen tells leaders coming to Francophonie Summit not to worry about border conflict

summary: Spokesperson Pen Bona stated the government is prioritizing both humanitarian aid for citizens affected by 'Thailand's acts of aggression' and diplomatic engagement through the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC). Cambodia remains committed to the December 27 ceasefire agreement despite ongoing challenges. The spokesperson emphasized that the administration is working to resolve issues faced by residents who have had their homes and property destroyed near the border.
title: Government Pursues Diplomacy Alongside Support for Border-Affected Citizens

summary: Nearly 600,000 Cambodians (92% of those displaced) have returned home since the December ceasefire, but 49,352 remain in camps. The Ministry of Interior reports that dozens of schools and health centers in Oddar Meanchey and Preah Vihear stay closed. The government accused Thailand of 'dishonest activities' like using containers and barbed wire to occupy areas Cambodia claims as its own.
title: 92% of displaced go home as border tensions persist

summary: UN Resident Coordinator Vladanka Andreeva met PM Hun Manet at the Peace Palace. She conveyed the UN's desire for a peaceful resolution to the border conflict according to international law. PM Hun Manet briefed her on recent developments and recalled his previous discussions with UN Secretary-General António Guterres. The meeting emphasized Cambodia's commitment to diplomatic solutions while maintaining its national interests.
title: UN Calls on Cambodia and Thailand to Resolve Border Issue in Line with UN Charter

summary: Cambodia formally accused Thailand of sustained military operations and harming civilians at the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva on March 2. The Cambodian envoy claimed Thai forces have caused casualties, destroyed homes, and led to large-scale displacement since May 2025, calling for international law to prevail over force.
title: Cambodia raises Thai border operations, harm to civilians, at UN Human Rights Council

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated that Prime Minister Hun Manet is actively briefing world leaders and UN officials on the border crisis. Cambodia continues to demand that Thailand respect the 1904-1907 Franco-Siamese maps. The government condemned the installation of barbed wire and shipping containers by Thai forces, describing them as illegal attempts to alter the border line and prevent tens of thousands of Cambodians from returning to their homes.
title: Cambodia Stands Firm on 'Rules-Based' Diplomacy Amid Border Standoff with Thailand

summary: Cambodian experts express concern that global attention on the US-Israel-Iran conflict is allowing Thailand to entrench its military positions along the border without international scrutiny. Analysts suggest Thailand may exploit this 'attention gap' to ignore MOU 2000 and other treaties. Meanwhile, the Royal Thai Army has warned it will strike deeper into Cambodia if long-range rocket launchers are deployed near the front lines.
title: Mideast war overshadows Cambodia-Thailand border row

source: Phnom Penh Post / Asia News Network
summary: OIF Secretary-General Louise Mushikiwabo visited the Wat Thormark Rangsey displacement camp in Siem Reap. The camp currently houses over 1,300 people who remain unable to return to their homes due to Thai military barricades, including shipping containers and razor wire, which reportedly remain despite the December 2025 ceasefire.
title: La Francophonie leader assesses Cambodia-Thailand border situation, visits displacement camps

summary: Deputy PM Prak Sokhonn visited displacement centers in Siem Reap to reassure 50,000 refugees that the government is seeking a non-violent end to the border dispute with Thailand. Officials reported that Thai troops are still occupying land in four provinces (Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Pursat) and using shipping containers to block roads. While 600,000 people have returned home since the conflict began, thousands remain in 'red zones' due to unexploded bombs and Thai military presence.
title: Govt assures displaced families of peaceful border solution

summary: Phay Siphan, Minister Attached to the Prime Minister, met with Malaysian embassy representatives to explain Cambodia's perspective on the border row. He accused Thailand of violating agreed legal frameworks and international law. The meeting is part of a broader Cambodian effort to inform regional neighbors (ASEAN) about Thai military 'encroachment' and to seek diplomatic support for a rules-based resolution.
title: Government official shows truth about Cambodia-Thailand border demarcation to Malaysian diplomat

summary: A delegation of 12 foreign military attachés visited Preah Vihear province to inspect unexploded ordnance (UXO). The Ministry of National Defence and CMAC reported finding 1,223 pieces of ordnance within the temple complex, which they claim were left by Thai military attacks during the 2025 escalation. The visit aims to document the impact on the UNESCO site.
title: Foreign Military Attachés Inspect Unexploded Ordnance at Preah Vihear Following Thai Attacks

summary: Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn addressed Cambodia's annual diplomatic conference, stating that the nation is facing 'aggression, territorial encroachment, and defamation' from a neighbor (referring to Thailand). He noted that Thai forces continue to occupy territory in Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Pursat following clashes in 2025. Sokhonn stated that Cambodia would not ask Thailand to reopen border checkpoints, asserting that it is up to Thailand to do so since they initiated the closures.
title: Diplomats urged to 'think outside the box' on national interests

summary: Several Cambodian travelers reported being denied entry and detained overnight at Don Mueang International Airport. Passengers claimed they were forced to pay 1,000 baht service fees and buy immediate return tickets without clear explanation. Some suspect the treatment is a form of retaliation or pressure related to the ongoing border conflict between the two nations.
title: Cambodian, Indian travellers report entry denial at Thai airport

summary: Oddar Meanchey Provincial Governor Mean Chanyada presided over a ceremony to distribute 203 newly built houses to displaced families in Samrong city and Banteay Ampil district. The governor stated these families were directly affected by the 'encirclement' of Thai troops. The housing project aims to provide stable living conditions for those who lost their homes during the border conflict.
title: 203 houses handed over to displaced families affected by Thai military encirclement

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that as of March 7, 2026, 46,394 people (including 24,326 women and 15,358 children) remain displaced and unable to return to their homes. While nearly 93% of the initial 640,000 displaced persons have returned following the December 27, 2025 ceasefire, the ministry accused Thailand of not fully complying with the General Border Committee (GBC) agreements and continuing 'insincere' activities despite mediation by international figures like Donald Trump and Anwar Ibrahim.
title: Ministry of Interior: 46,394 displaced persons still unable to return home

summary: Secretary of State Chan Narith of the Ministry of Economy and Finance announced that a government working group is collaborating with diplomatic missions and development partners to rehabilitate infrastructure damaged by 'Thai aggression.' Priority is being given to repairing roads, bridges, schools, and hospitals to facilitate the return of displaced communities. The official emphasized the need for international assistance to address the long-term impact of the shelling on border infrastructure.
title: Rehabilitation efforts underway for families displaced by Cambodian–Thai border conflict

summary: The Cambodian government has begun distributing provisional shelters to families displaced by ongoing border tensions. These families' homes were either destroyed or are located in areas currently occupied by Thai military forces. The move aims to provide stability for those who cannot yet return to their original villages due to safety concerns and the presence of foreign troops.
title: Government Hands Over Shelters to Border Families Displaced by Thai Aggression

summary: Cambodian delegates at international forums, including the UN Human Rights Council, are reporting on Thai military actions. Specifically, they highlight the occupation of nearly 800 hectares in Banteay Meanchey (Prey Chan and Chokchey villages) and the recent arrest of three Cambodian fishermen near Koh Yor, demanding their immediate release.
title: Cambodia continues to expose Thai aggression on major international platforms while stakeholders promise to monitor

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that safeguarding territorial integrity is the top priority. He reported that tens of thousands of Cambodians are still unable to return to their homes due to Thai military obstacles like barbed wire and shipping containers. Currently, about 45,000 people remain in temporary shelters. Cambodia insists on following the French-era maps and does not recognize any border changes made by force.
title: Cambodia Vows 'Relentless' Defence of Sovereignty Amid Thai Border Strains

summary: Political observers and opposition figures, including Um Sam An, have criticized PM Hun Manet for failing to reclaim 45 sites allegedly occupied by Thailand. They argue that while the government promotes 'Nokor Sangkranta' celebrations, soldiers are dying and civilians remain in camps. Critics are urging the government to file a case against Thailand at the International Court of Justice (ICJ).
title: Hun Manet has been criticized for not daring to sue Thailand for the sake of territorial defense even though Thailand has increased its aggression

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona announced that Cambodia is actively fighting a 'diplomatic battle' against Thai military aggression. He claimed that Thai forces continue to build infrastructure and use barbed wire and shipping containers to block tens of thousands of displaced Cambodians from returning to their homes in border provinces like Preah Vihear and Banteay Meanchey.
title: Government says barbed wire and Thai containers still pose obstacles threatening tens of thousands of Cambodian citizens

summary: Ly Thuch, First Vice-President of the CMAA, stated that 'ongoing border tension' and incomplete demarcation are complicating efforts to clear landmines along the Thai-Cambodian border. He noted that rugged terrain and the sensitive political situation create uncertainties for survey teams. The report mentions that hostilities from 2025 resulted in about 400,000 hectares of territory contaminated with unexploded ordnance.
title: Border tensions may slow de-mining action, says CMAA

summary: The Cambodian government is urging citizens to trust its 'quiet diplomacy' strategy. This comes as opposition figures criticize the government for failing to remove Thai troops from areas Cambodia claims. PM Hun Manet stated that while they can't reveal every move, the goal is to avoid another war while gaining international support for Cambodian sovereignty. The government confirmed it has notified the UN Security Council and ASEAN observers about Thai military incursions.
title: Govt defends 'quiet diplomacy' to resolve border spat

summary: Local media highlights PM Hun Manet's recent engagement with international journalists as a strategic move to show the world evidence of Thai military 'aggression.' The reporting frames the conflict as a premeditated plan by Thailand to seize Cambodian territory and calls for international pressure on Bangkok.
title: Cambodian PM's interview is a message to the world to bear witness to Thai aggression

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow has responded to Cambodia's urgent request for a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting by stating that procedures must wait until the new Thai government is officially formed. Cambodia had previously sent a note verbale proposing an emergency meeting in Siem Reap to discuss temporary boundary markers between pillars 42-47 and 52-59. The report notes that Thailand needs more time for internal legal procedures before resuming land boundary negotiations.
title: Thailand says JBC meeting will wait for new government

summary: The Royal Government of Cambodia has dismissed Thai media reports suggesting Prime Minister Hun Manet agreed to delay border talks until after the Khmer New Year in April. The spokesperson clarified that Cambodia has already submitted five formal requests for immediate technical and high-level meetings. This follows the 2025 border clashes, with Cambodia insisting on using established bilateral mechanisms to resolve the illegal occupation of territory by Thai forces.
title: Govt Spokesperson Denies Thai Claim Border Talks Will Happen After Khmer New Year

summary: The Thai government has issued a formal ban on recruiting new Cambodian migrant workers, citing "national security risks" linked to the ongoing border tensions. Despite pleas from Thailand's private sector regarding labor shortages in construction and agriculture, Thai Labor Minister Treenuch Thienthong confirmed the government will only manage existing permit holders. Cambodian officials downplayed the impact on the domestic labor market, though researchers note that many workers who fled previous clashes remain in debt and struggle to find work at home.
title: Thai Blocks New Cambodian Workers Over Security Risk, but Officials Say it Won’t Affect Cambodia

summary: Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn briefed Singaporean leaders on the situation of displaced Cambodian civilians who cannot return home due to Thai military presence and barriers. The diplomatic strategy aims to 'strengthen old friendships' to ensure territorial integrity while adhering to peaceful resolution mechanisms like the Joint Boundary Committee.
title: Cambodia Prioritises Diplomatic Offensive Amid Thai Border Tensions

summary: Government Spokesperson Pen Bona highlighted Cambodia's active international diplomacy to address the border conflict with Thailand. Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn recently raised concerns at the 61st UN Human Rights Council session in Geneva regarding the humanitarian impact of Thai military presence in Cambodian villages. He also discussed the border situation and the plight of displaced civilians during a visit to Singapore on March 11. The government stresses that protecting territorial integrity remains the highest priority while seeking peaceful diplomatic solutions.
title: Diplomatic Missions Reflect Strengthening Old Friendships and Expanding New Ones

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona has formally dismissed reports from Thai media alleging that Prime Minister Hun Manet proposed delaying Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) talks until after the Khmer New Year in April. Cambodia maintains that it has already submitted five requests to Thailand to resume survey work and install temporary markers in areas such as Banteay Meanchey and Battambang, which remain partly occupied by Thai forces. The spokesperson emphasized that Cambodia is ready to resume talks immediately and is not waiting for the holiday period.
title: Cambodia rebuts Thai media claims on border talks

summary: Information Minister Neth Pheaktra accused Thailand of using a 'fake news strategy' to justify military aggression. He claimed Thailand fabricates stories about online scam centers and landmines to launch airstrikes and incursions. The Minister urged local media to be cautious when reporting news from Thai sources, which he characterized as propaganda aimed at obscuring territorial violations.
title: Minister Neth Pheaktra says Thailand uses fake news as an excuse to invade Cambodia

summary: Cambodia has lodged a formal protest against Thai military construction and excavation near the Preah Vihear Temple and Ta Krabey Temple. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs claims these actions violate the 1962 and 2013 International Court of Justice rulings. Specific violations include building a guard post, a road toward Keo Sikha Kiri Svarak Pagoda, and a large Buddha statue in contested areas.
title: Cambodia protests unlawful activities by Thai military

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a clarification following a Thai press release that called for Cambodia's 'good-faith cooperation' in land demarcation. Cambodia rejected the Thai narrative, reaffirming its commitment to international law and existing treaties while accusing Thailand of misrepresenting the border survey progress.
title: Foreign Ministry issues statement rejecting false Thai claims

summary: Keo Remy, Chairman of the Cambodia Human Rights Committee, briefed UN Resident Coordinator Vladanka Andreeva on the border situation. He accused the Thai military of violating international law, including violence against Cambodian migrant workers, using high-decibel sound to disturb residents, and conducting indiscriminate attacks with heavy weapons and cluster bombs against civilians.
title: Keo Remy tells UN: Cambodia's position is to resolve border peacefully

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest on Friday against Thai military construction in disputed areas. Cambodia claims Thai personnel are building a large Buddha statue in the Bosbov-Choam Tae area and permanent infrastructure like concrete roads near the Preah Vihear and Ta Krabey temples. The ministry stated these actions violate the 1962 and 2013 ICJ rulings and the 2000 MOU by unilaterally altering the border environment.
title: Cambodia lodges protest over Thai border construction activities

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs lodged a formal protest against Thai military activities between Feb 23 and March 7, 2026. Allegations include illegal construction and excavation at the Preah Vihear temple promontory, a new guard post, and a road toward Keo Sikha Kiri Svarak Pagoda. They also accuse Thai forces of building a large Buddha statue in the Bosbov-Choam Tae area and permanent infrastructure at Ta Krabey Temple.
title: Cambodia protests strongly against illegal actions of Thai armed forces violating sovereignty

summary: Reporters visiting Banteay Meanchey province observed that the Thai military has placed 105 shipping containers across 20 locations in Boeng Trakuon, Choke Chey, and Prey Chan villages. Local officials claim Thailand is occupying 760 hectares of Cambodian land illegally, preventing residents from returning home despite a ceasefire agreement signed in December 2025. The area, once bustling, is now described as a ghost town surrounded by barbed wire.
title: Update on Boeng Trakuon, Choke Chey, and Prey Chan: Thai military illegally occupies land with containers after ceasefire

summary: Photos released by Fresh News and shared by Khmer Times show Thai forces allegedly annexing Cambodian territory in Banteay Meanchey province. The images depict the Thai military installing over 100 shipping containers as blockades in O Chrov and Thma Puok districts. The report claims widespread destruction of property by Thai forces.
title: IN PICTURES: Thailand annexes Cambodian land

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a clarification on Friday regarding a Thai press release from March 11. Cambodia officially denied a Thai report claiming Cambodian forces fired a 40-mm grenade into Thai territory on February 24, 2026. The ministry stated that this was verified as false by military liaison teams from both sides. Cambodia urged Thailand to show 'good-faith cooperation' and 'sincerity' instead of circulating incorrect reports that could lead to misunderstandings.
title: Cambodia responds to Thai statement on border demarcation

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona announced that Cambodia is engaging in 'active and uninterrupted' diplomatic missions to protect its borders from Thai military violations. This includes legal challenges and international advocacy during Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn's tour of Singapore, New Zealand, and Australia. The government emphasizes that while it seeks peace, it is ready to exercise its right to self-defense.
title: Cambodia Vows 'Uninterrupted' Diplomacy to Defend Sovereignty After Thai Incursions

summary: Authorities have uncovered more than 1,300 items of unexploded ordnance, identified as Thai bombs, in the vicinity of the Preah Vihear Temple. The discovery follows intense military activity in the area during previous clashes. The report highlights the ongoing danger to civilians and heritage sites due to military munitions left behind in disputed zones.
title: IN PICTURES: Over 1300 Thai bombs found at Preah Vihear Temple, so far

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated that Cambodia is maintaining its diplomatic stance and continues to protest against Thai military actions. Specifically, Cambodia objects to the installation of container blockades, the construction of roads and trenches, and the use of drones by Thai forces in border areas. These actions are described as preventing Cambodian citizens from returning to their homes and violating international law.
title: Pen Bona: Royal Government of Cambodia continues diplomatic action and protests against Thai activities along the border

summary: Minister Delegate Jean-François Tăn used strong language on social media to condemn Thai military presence on Cambodian soil, calling it a violation of sovereignty. He characterized Thailand's actions as those of a 'new colonial country' and claimed that Thailand's use of airstrikes was a sign of failure in ground combat. He called for international sanctions against Thailand for the destruction of world heritage property.
title: Jean-François Tăn: Thailand is a new colonial country that sits on international law

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona detailed 'illegal' Thai military actions from late February to mid-March, including excavations near Preah Vihear and the installation of Thai flags and concrete roads in Oddar Meanchey. The government called on Thailand to stop these activities immediately and respect the December 27, 2025 ceasefire agreement, stressing that Cambodia will not recognize any border changes made by force.
title: Press Briefing by H.E. Pen Bona on the latest developments along the Cambodia-Thailand border

summary: During a meeting with the Danish Ambassador, Senate President Hun Sen reaffirmed that the Cambodian government strictly adheres to the December 27, 2025 ceasefire agreement. He emphasized that Cambodia seeks a peaceful resolution through negotiations based on international law, despite the current tensions along the border.
title: Denmark Pleased with Cambodia’s Position on Resolving Border Dispute with Thailand

summary: Phnom Penh has filed a formal diplomatic protest against the Thai military for building roads and a large Buddha statue in contested border areas near Preah Vihear Temple. Cambodian officials claim these activities violate the 2000 MOU and International Court of Justice rulings. The border remains closed, and roughly 950,000 Cambodian workers have fled Thailand since late 2025 due to security fears.
title: Cambodia protests Thailand’s ‘illegal’ constructions around Preah Vihear and contested areas

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated that Cambodia is prioritizing a 'diplomatic offensive' to secure international support regarding border tensions. Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn has been briefing counterparts in Singapore and Australia about the situation, including the plight of displaced Cambodian civilians who cannot return to their border homes.
title: Cambodia vows ‘uninterrupted’ diplomacy to defend sovereignty

summary: The article reports on growing domestic criticism from Cambodian intellectuals and activists. They express concern that the current administration under PM Hun Manet is not being firm enough against Thai 'encroachment' and infrastructure development in disputed border zones, fearing a loss of territorial integrity.
title: Some Cambodian intellectuals are disappointed that Hun Manet is allowing Thailand to take Cambodian land as it pleases

summary: A public clarification was issued regarding Thai plans to build fences and roads between markers 52 and 59 in Battambang province. Sources state that since locations were agreed upon in 2008 and temporary markers were set in late 2025, construction within Thai territory is not a violation. However, it warns that any activity in unagreed segments would breach international law and the 2000 MOU.
title: Border plans between markers 52–59 clarified amid Thai construction concerns

summary: The Cambodian Foreign Ministry has protested against Thai military occupation of 15 locations on Cambodian soil. Despite the December 27 ceasefire, Phnom Penh claims Thai forces remain in areas belonging to the Kingdom and are carrying out illegal infrastructure activities.
title: Foreign ministry reissues call for Thais to cease 'illegal activities' on Kingdom's soil

summary: The Cambodian government has listed several specific border locations where they say Thai soldiers are violating sovereignty. Reports mention Thai monks and soldiers together erecting Buddha statues in disputed areas like Ta Thav and An Seh. The protest notes that these actions violate the 1904 and 1907 Franco-Siamese treaties which Cambodia uses to define its borders.
title: Cambodia lodges formal protest against Thailand’s continued encroachment and unlawful land occupation

summary: Thai lawmakers are voting for a new PM, with incumbent Anutin Charnvirakul likely to win. Anutin’s campaign focused heavily on being a 'defender of the nation' during the 2025 border conflict with Cambodia. This nationalist stance helped his party win 191 seats. The previous PM, Paetongtarn Shinawatra, was ousted partly due to her handling of the border crisis.
title: Thai Parliament Convenes To Vote for New Prime Minister

summary: Official sources in Cambodia are monitoring Thai movements in Sa Kaeo province near the Banteay Meanchey border. Reports indicate Thai forces are measuring land and have finished building 38 bomb shelters, with 100 more planned. Cambodia views these as attempts to create a 'fait accompli' (permanent fact) on the ground in territories it considers unlawfully occupied since the clashes in December 2025.
title: Calls for restraint over reported Thai military activities in unlawfully occupied areas

summary: Since Thailand closed the border crossings, Thai goods are reportedly being rerouted through the Trapeang Kriel International Border Checkpoint from Laos. While authorities state they cannot legally block these imports due to WTO and ASEAN rules, they are urging Cambodian citizens to boycott products from the 'aggressor country' as a nationalist measure.
title: Thai goods enter Cambodia via Laos amid border closure

summary: Phnom Penh has officially protested against what it calls the 'unlawful occupation' of land by Thai forces. Despite a ceasefire signed on December 27, 2025, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs claims Thai troops are still clearing land and building permanent structures like roads and bunkers in Preah Vihear and Oddar Meanchey. Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that Cambodia will never accept border changes made by force.
title: Cambodia files protest over Thai military activity on its territory

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated that the upcoming 'Nokor Songkran' festival will be a significant display of national unity. He linked the cultural celebration to the bravery of Cambodian heroes and the current need for solidarity, especially as the country faces ongoing challenges along its borders. The message emphasizes that Khmer culture and sovereignty are inseparable.
title: Mr. Pen Bona: 'Nokor Songkran' program is an opportunity to show strong Khmer national unity

summary: The Cambodian government has issued an urgent appeal to Thailand to follow existing border agreements after reports of Thai military activities in disputed zones. Phnom Penh has requested five meetings of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) so far in 2026, but Bangkok has reportedly postponed every session, citing internal political transitions after their February elections. Cambodian officials warn that unilateral actions like building fences or infrastructure in unagreed areas violate the 2000 MoU.
title: Cambodia calls on Thailand to adhere to frontier treaties

summary: A new research report highlights that a surge in nationalist anger on platforms like TikTok and Facebook served as a digital precursor to the armed conflict that erupted in July 2025. Experts warn that while military ceasefires are in place, the 'digital battleground' remains active, with citizens from both sides continuing to argue over cultural heritage and history, which prevents real healing between the two nations.
title: Online hostility spiked between Cambodians and Thais before outbreak of war, study finds

summary: A commentary by lawyer Long Panhavuth critiquing ASEAN's failure to mediate the 2025-2026 border conflict. The piece argues that nationalist Thai politics and ASEAN's non-interference policy led to military escalation, the weaponization of migrant livelihoods, and the need for external global power intervention.
title: The ASEAN Illusion: Legal and Human Casualties of the Thai-Cambodian Crisis

summary: The Cambodian government has reiterated that it will not recognize any border maps or land claims made unilaterally by Thailand. Officials called for an immediate end to Thai military encroachment in areas like Boeng Trakuon and Ou Teuk Choul, where smoke was seen rising from houses currently under Thai occupation. Reports also indicated Thai officials were measuring and dividing land for Thai citizens in Banteay Meanchey province between border markers 46 and 47 on March 18.
title: Cambodia states it will not accept any border lines or territorial claims based on unilateral assertions by Thailand

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest on March 20 against Thai armed forces for violating sovereignty. Reports include smoke from burning houses in the Boeung Trakuon area under Thai occupation, and illegal road construction/land clearing by Thai troops in Oddar Meanchey province. Cambodia stated it will not recognize any unilateral boundary lines or territorial claims asserted by Thailand.
title: Phnom Penh objects to Thai military moves on Cambodian territory

summary: The Cambodian government lodged a formal protest against Thai armed forces for violating sovereignty after the Dec 27, 2025 ceasefire. Reports claim Thai forces burned houses in the Boeung Trakuon area and, on March 18, 2026, began measuring and dividing land for Thai citizens in O'Beichoan commune, Banteay Meanchey. Cambodia maintains it does not recognize unilateral Thai border claims.
title: Cambodia officially protests against new Thai activities violating border sovereignty

summary: According to a Ministry of Foreign Affairs press release on March 20, Cambodia has filed a new formal protest against Thai armed forces for violating sovereignty and territorial integrity following the December 27, 2025 ceasefire. Violations were reported at Boeng Trakuon, where three residential locations were seen burning, and at Ou Teuk Choul, where Thai forces continued clearing land and constructing concrete roads towards Ta Krabey Temple.
title: Cambodia rejects border lines or territorial claims from unilateral Thai assertions

summary: Nearly 3,000 families displaced from the Boeung Trakuon area due to Thai military occupation have begun relocating to temporary shelters. The first phase involves 800 families moving to Slakram village, where the government has built 5x7 meter houses on 20x30 meter plots. The site includes a school and health center to support those unable to return home since the December 2025 border tensions.
title: Deputy governor: 3,000 displaced families to be relocated, first 800 begin move in Banteay Meanchey

summary: Japanese Ambassador Ueno Atsushi announced that Japan has provided approximately $17 million in emergency aid since the conflict began in mid-2025. This includes $1.8 million for displaced people at the border and support for Cambodian migrant workers returning from Thailand. Japan also provided 30 new mine detectors worth $1.3 million to assist in demining efforts near the border.
title: Since the Cambodia-Thailand conflict in 2025, Japan has provided nearly $20 million in aid to Cambodians

summary: Three months after a ceasefire, the Preah Vihear Temple remains closed to tourists due to extensive damage from artillery and the presence of unexploded ordnance (UXO). Cambodian officials report that the 11th-century UNESCO site suffers from unstable walls and craters. Once a popular destination, the site is now roped off with landmine warning signs, reflecting the severe physical toll of the border conflict on cultural heritage.
title: A 1,000-Year-Old Temple Lies Battered After Cambodia-Thailand Border Clashes

summary: Government Spokesman Pen Bona stated that protecting territorial integrity is Cambodia's highest priority. Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn has briefed international partners, including high-ranking diplomats from India, Singapore, and the EU, on the border situation. The government highlighted the plight of tens of thousands of displaced Cambodian civilians who cannot return home due to the ongoing tensions.
title: Cambodia Reaffirms Territorial Integrity, Elevates Border Developments as Top Diplomatic Priority

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona issued a statement on March 24 emphasizing that the Cambodian government maintains the protection of territorial integrity and its people as its highest priority. This follows ongoing concerns regarding the border situation with Thailand.
title: Government Spokesman Pen Bona: The Government Never Forgets Duty to Protect Territory and People

summary: Tensions and disruptions at the Thai-Cambodian border have caused a 37.8% decline in land-based tourist arrivals. Industry experts cite the unstable security situation as a primary deterrent for international travelers visiting historical sites like Angkor Wat and Preah Vihear.
title: Kingdom records huge drop in foreign tourist arrivals

summary: Three months after a ceasefire, Preah Vihear temple remains severely damaged and closed to tourists due to artillery craters and unexploded ordnance. Cambodian officials warn structures are in danger of collapse during the upcoming rainy season, accusing the Thai military of deliberate attacks during the 2025 conflict.
title: A 1,000-year-old cliff-top temple lies battered after Cambodia-Thailand border clashes

summary: The Documentation Center of Cambodia (DC-Cam) has begun a mission to document evidence of the 2025 border conflict. They are interviewing displaced villagers and gathering data on what they term the Thai 'invasion' to preserve a historical record for future legal or diplomatic use.
title: DC-Cam records border conflict to uphold truth and justice

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of National Defence has dismissed claims by a Thai army intelligence chief that a 'third conflict' is likely in late 2026. Thai Lt Gen Theeranan Nanthakwang reportedly warned that Cambodia's 2027 elections and arms purchases could trigger fighting. Cambodian spokesperson Maly Socheata called these reports 'incorrect and baseless,' asserting that Cambodian forces strictly follow the December 2025 peace agreements and international law.
title: Thailand Warns of Third Border Conflict in Claim Cambodia Rejects

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence has officially dismissed reports from Thai media claiming that Cambodia is preparing for a 'third armed conflict.' Spokeswoman Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata stated these claims, allegedly from Thai intelligence, are baseless and do not reflect the reality on the ground. She reaffirmed that the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces are adhering to the December 2025 peace agreements and remain committed to a peaceful resolution of border issues.
title: Cambodia Rejects Thai Media Claims of Third Armed Conflict as 'Incorrect and Baseless'

summary: Cambodian officials and international relations experts have accused the Thai military of a 'calculated annexation strategy' by establishing 'facts on the ground.' Despite a ceasefire effective since December 2025, reports indicate Thai forces are moving into Cambodian territory in Banteay Meanchey and settling civilians there. As of March 23, over 36,000 Cambodians remain displaced, unable to return to homes blocked by Thai barbed wire and containers.
title: Thai actions at border a 'calculated annexation strategy'

summary: A detailed damage assessment of the Preah Vihear Temple reveals the site was hit in 420 locations during heavy fighting in December 2025. All five gateway pavilions are damaged, and experts warn some structures may collapse in the upcoming rainy season. Cambodia's Information Minister Neth Pheaktra accused the Thai military of deliberately targeting the UNESCO World Heritage site, while Thailand claims the site was militarized by Cambodian forces.
title: 1,000-year-old temple lies battered after Cambodia-Thai border clashes

summary: Royal Government Spokesperson H.E. Pen Bona briefed the media on Cambodia’s continued commitment to the General Border Committee (GBC) spirit. He emphasized that Cambodia strictly follows the December 27, 2025, Joint Statement, which focuses on peaceful dispute resolution and avoiding the use of force. The briefing served to reiterate Cambodia's stance on maintaining current border positions while pushing for technical surveys via the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC).
title: Cambodian Government Spokesperson Reaffirms Joint Commitment with Thailand in GBC Spirit

summary: In an official statement, the MFAIC spokesperson welcomed a recent joint information center statement that aligns with international law. Cambodia emphasized that the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) remains the only authoritative body to define the border and expressed readiness to resume work immediately based on historical treaties.
title: Cambodia Reaffirms Commitment to Peaceful Border Resolution with Thailand

summary: The Ministry of National Defence has labeled claims by Thai Army Intelligence Chief, Lt. Gen. Teeranan Nandhakwang, as 'incorrect and baseless.' The Thai official had alleged that Cambodia is preparing for a third round of armed conflict. Ministry spokeswoman Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata stated that Cambodia remains committed to the December 27, 2025, ceasefire and urged the public to ignore unsubstantiated rumors that could destabilize the border region.
title: Cambodia rejects Thai military leader's allegations that it's preparing for another round of armed clashes

summary: The Cambodian Mine Action Centre (CMAC) reports that over 2,360 square kilometers of land along the Thai border are contaminated with cluster munitions. An estimated 6 to 7 million bomblets were fired into residential areas, farms, and schools during recent conflicts. Seven provinces, including Banteay Meanchey and Preah Vihear, are severely affected, posing a lethal risk to returning displaced civilians.
title: CMAC reports massive scale of cluster munition contamination along Thai border

summary: Cambodian military authorities in the Thma Da area of Pursat province have officially rejected claims by Thai Marine Task Force commanders alleging that Cambodian troops committed 'repeated provocations' and gunfire breaches over the past week. Cambodian officials stated they strictly adhere to the December 27, 2025 ceasefire and follow government directives to maintain peace. They dismissed the Thai reports as 'inaccurate and misleading' attempts to create tension.
title: Cambodian Forces Deny Thai Claims of Border Provocations in Pursat

summary: The State Secretariat of Border Affairs (SSBA) officially rejected a recommendation from a Thai Senate ad hoc committee to scrap the 2000 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on border demarcation. Cambodia argues that the proposal is politically motivated and violates international law. Officials stated that the MOU remains the legal foundation for resolving border disputes and that any unilateral cancellation would be invalid under global treaties.
title: Cambodia Rejects Thai Senate Call to Revoke MOU 2000, Citing International Law

summary: The Cambodian State Secretariat of Border Affairs has 'entirely dismissed' a recommendation from a Thai Senate ad hoc committee to revoke the 2000 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU 2000) on border demarcation. Cambodian officials labeled the move as 'unfounded, politically motivated, and contrary to international law.' They argued that unilateral revocation would violate the principle of 'uti possidetis juris' (the inviolability of inherited borders) and hinder peaceful resolution efforts.
title: Cambodia Rejects Thai Senate’s Call to Scrap Border MoU

summary: Local media reports that Thai troops moved to install national flags and shipping containers in the Thmar Da area to expand their presence while foreign diplomats were visiting the site. The report also mentions claims from the Cambodian Mine Action Centre (CMAC) that Thai forces used approximately 130,000 cluster bombs during the recent conflict.
title: កម្មវិធី កម្ពុជាថ្មី Realtime ថ្ងៃទី27 ខែមីនា ឆ្នាំ2026

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFAIC) issued a statement on March 26 calling for the immediate resumption of joint technical surveys via the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to permanently demarcate the frontier. This follows a March 19 statement from a joint info center. Cambodia urged a move from 'diplomatic words' to concrete action to prevent future military friction and achieve lasting peace based on historical 1904 and 1907 treaties.
title: Cambodia calls for ‘substantive’ action on Thailand border demarcation

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that since the ceasefire took effect on December 27, 2025, Cambodia has successfully maintained peace for three months. He emphasized that the government continues to exercise its right to resolve border issues with Thailand through peaceful negotiations despite recent challenges. The statement serves as an official progress report on the post-conflict stability period.
title: Three months of ceasefire: Cambodia maintains full right to peaceful border resolution

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn led a group of foreign diplomats and UN representatives to Thmor Da commune in Pursat province to show areas allegedly illegally occupied by Thai forces. He observed that Thai military personnel have installed containers and barbed wire in the area. Sokhonn reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to resolving the dispute through peaceful means and bilateral agreements, specifically citing the Joint Statement from December 2025.
title: DPM Prak Sokhonn Reaffirms Peaceful Resolution of Border Issues in Accordance with International Law

summary: អ្នកវិភាគច្បាប់មើលឃើញថា ថៃហាក់ដូចជាបានសម្រេចចិត្តប្រើប្រាស់កម្លាំងយោធា ដើម្បីឈ្លានពានកម្ពុជា ដោយបានលុបចោលអនុស្សរណៈយោគយល់គ្នា (MoU) ឆ្នាំ 2000 ទៅហើយ។ ទង្វើនេះអាចបង្កជាមហន្តរាយធំដល់ប្រទេសទាំងពីរ ព្រោះកម្ពុជាក៏ប្រហែលជាមិននៅស្ងៀមដែរ បើថៃបើកការវាយប្រហារមែននោះ។
title: ថៃពង្រីកការឈ្លានពានឥតឈប់ខណៈកម្ពុជាបន្តបោះដៃរកការចរចាដោយសន្តិវិធី

summary: កម្ពុជាកំពុងសម្របសម្រួលជាមួយក្រុមអ្នកសង្កេតការណ៍អាស៊ាន (AOT) ដើម្បីចុះពិនិត្យមើលស្ថានភាពនៅតាមព្រំដែនតំបន់ភូមិព្រៃចាន់។ ការចុះពិនិត្យនេះធ្វើឡើងស្របពេលដែលថៃបានយកទូកុងតឺណ័រមករារាំង និងរំលោភយកដីខ្មែរជាង 584 ហិកតានៅតំបន់បឹងត្រកួន។
title: កម្ពុជាសម្របសម្រួលក្រុម AOT ចុះពិនិត្យស្ថានភាពព្រំដែន នៅតំបន់ភូមិព្រៃចាន់

summary: At 9:33 AM on Sunday, March 29, the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) conducted a mission at the O'Smach International Border Checkpoint in Oddar Meanchey province. Lieutenant General Maly Socheata, spokeswoman for the Ministry of National Defence, stated that the Thai army has illegally occupied part of this area since late December 2025. Specifically, Thai troops are reported to have encroached 420 meters into Cambodian territory. Cambodia reaffirmed its commitment to the 2025 peace agreements and stated its goal is to restore normalcy through the coordination of the ASEAN team.
title: Cambodia Reaffirms Commitment to Border Peace as AOT Monitors Illegal Occupation at O'Smach International Border Checkpoint

summary: Cambodian local media published an analysis alleging that the Thai military-backed government is manufacturing a border defense crisis and initiating an 'illegal invasion of Cambodian territory' to distract the Thai public from its severe domestic economic stagnation, rising household debt, and political instability. The report claims the conflict has displaced over half a million Cambodians and damaged local civilian infrastructure.
title: Price of distraction: Thailand's manufactured hegemony and domestic policy failure reality

summary: High-ranking military officials visited front-line troops to boost morale before the Khmer New Year. Amidst the visit, officials addressed claims regarding the destruction of Khmer temples along the border by Thai forces. The government spokesperson also denied Thai claims that border talks would only happen after the New Year, stating that Cambodia has already submitted five specific requests for negotiation.
title: General Thet Visits Border Forces in Military Region 5 Ahead of Khmer New Year

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation strongly rejected claims that Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn suggested Cambodia would cede land to Thailand. During a visit to displaced residents in Pursat, Sokhonn stated that Cambodia is committed to peaceful legal mechanisms based on 1904 and 1907 treaties, while accusing Thailand of relying on military power. The ministry clarified that any encroachment found during demarcation must be returned on a reciprocal basis.
title: Cambodia Rejects 'Distorted' Claims of Ceding Land to Thailand

summary: Thai naval authorities removed Captain Thammanoon Wanna, commander of special forces in Trat, and 17 other officers following a heated verbal dispute with Cambodian troops. The conflict began on March 26 at the Thmor Da border crossing over the placement of a Thai flag on a container. A negotiation expert, Colonel Pratchaya Phoyoy, has been appointed to replace him to ease regional tensions and prioritize diplomacy over military force.
title: ថៃដកតំណែងមេបញ្ជាការជើងទឹកម្នាក់ ក្រោយផ្ទុះជម្លោះពាក្យសម្តីជាមួយទាហានកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Thai Navy Commander Removed After Verbal Conflict with Cambodian Soldiers
